title: Vietnam's textile boom may not translate into apparel growth
content:
Vietnam’s textile and garment exports reached $4,672 million in July 2026, up 4.3 per cent year on year; the seven-month total was $27.02 billion, up 2.67 per cent.
Growth was concentrated upstream as garments, the volume anchor, grew just 0.7 per cent.
Vietnam faces a 20 per cent US apparel tariff, while US apparel imports from Vietnam rose only 1.4 per cent in January–May 2026.

title: India ITME 2026 roadshow begins with Coimbatore curtain-raiser
content:
India ITME Society has launched its campaign for India ITME 2026 with a curtain-raiser in Coimbatore.
Scheduled for December 4–9 in Greater Noida, the event expects over 1,800 exhibitors, participation from 95-plus countries and over 150,000 visitors.
It will showcase advanced textile machinery, sustainable manufacturing and next-generation technologies.

title: India's Q1 FY27 GDP growth seen at 8%: SBI Research
content:
SBI Research expects India’s real GDP growth at about 8 per cent in Q1 FY27, above the RBI projection of 7 per cent.
The nowcast cites broad-based momentum, with 86 per cent of over 50 leading indicators accelerating versus 69 per cent a year earlier.
For textile exporters and apparel sourcing teams, resilient demand, capex and credit trends point to a supportive near-term market.

title: India loses $1.25 bn in T&A export orders from US in H1 2026
content:
India’s T&A exports to the US fell 23.3 per cent YoY to around $4.10 billion in H1 2026, from $5.35 billion a year earlier. 
Its calculated US import-market share slipped to around 8.6 per cent from 10.4 per cent, a loss of about 1.8 percentage points. 
ASEAN shipments rose 4.5 per cent to $15.34 billion, while Bangladesh marginally exceeded India at around $4.12 billion.

title: India retains BBB- rating as Fitch flags robust growth prospects
content:
Fitch affirmed India’s BBB- sovereign rating with a Stable Outlook, citing robust growth, solid external finances and stability.
For textile and apparel exporters, manufacturers and sourcing teams, this points to resilient growth and contained inflation.
FY27 GDP growth is forecast at 6.4 per cent and inflation at 4.1 per cent, while energy shocks, high debt and debt service remain constraints.

title: Adopt fair trading practices to take 'Make in India' global: Goyal
content:
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal urged fair trading practices, recycling, reuse and circular-economy participation to strengthen the Make in India brand globally.
He said nine free trade agreements have opened markets for Indian industry, supporting preferential access for exporters and MSMEs.
With exports at a record $863 trillion last year, Goyal set a $1 trillion target for the current year.

title: Bangladesh AmCham targets over $5 bn in US investment
content:
AmCham Bangladesh aims to mobilise over $5 billion in extra US investment over five years for Bangladesh’s investment pipeline.
It backed FY2026-27 reforms on approvals, Single Window, tax, VAT, repatriation and customs, while seeking policy predictability.
For apparel and textile sourcing chains, the US-Bangladesh trade framework could support stronger global value-chain positioning.

title: US' Kontoor Brands Q2 revenue up 19% on Helly Hansen boost
content:
American apparel and workwear group Kontoor Brands reported a 19 per cent YoY rise in Q2 FY26 revenue to $584 million, supported by Helly Hansen and Wrangler growth. 
Adjusted operating income increased 19 per cent to $94 million, while EPS rose 13 per cent to $1.06. 
The company raised its FY26 outlook, projecting revenue of $2.66–2.71 billion and higher adjusted EPS.

title: Bangladesh apparel suppliers press US buyers on tariff refunds
content:
Bangladeshi garment exporters are pressing US buyers for compensation after absorbing part of 2025 reciprocal tariff costs through price cuts and discounts. 
US importers are receiving refunds after the Supreme Court ruled against the tariff regime. 
Suppliers may seek recovery through higher prices, larger orders, concessions or legal claims under LDP terms.

title: India’s 95% compliance bet meets $11 bn apparel export stakes
content:
India has raised TRACE support for export testing and certification, with micro and small enterprises eligible for up to 95 per cent of costs and medium enterprises up to 80 per cent.
TexPro shows the US, EU and UK absorbed $10.99 billion, or 69.5 per cent, of India’s apparel exports in FY2025-26.
EU product passport work and the ban on destroying unsold apparel underline rising compliance
